edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo. Simplicitas, bonitas, habitet in corpore vestro. Irasci nolite sine causa fratri devoto: Recipietis enim quidquid feceritis ab illo. Hoc placuit Christo, resurgere mortuos, imo, Cum suis corporibus, et quos ignis ussit in aevo, Sex millibus annis completis mundo finito. Vertitur interea coelum tenore mutato: Comburuntur enim impii tunc igne divino. Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo. Digniores, stemmate et generati praeclaro, Nobilesque viri sub Antichristo devicto: Ex praecepto Dei rursum viventes in aevo, Mille quidem annis ut serviant sanctis et Alto, Sub jugo servili, ut portent victualia collo; Ut iterum autem judicentur regno finito. Nullificantes Deum, completo millesimo anno, Ab igne peribunt, cum montibus ipsi loquendo. In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto, Demerguntur inferno, trahunt poenas in aevo. Ostenduntur illis, et legunt gesta de coelo Memoria prisca debito et merita digno. Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno. Omnia non possum comprehendere parvo libello. Curiositas docti inveniet nomen in isto.
pass_a_gloss: Inhabitants of heaven future with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Simplicity, goodness, let it dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother: for you will receive whatever you do from him. This pleased Christ, to resurrect the dead, indeed, with their bodies, and those whom fire has burned in the age, six thousand years completed world finished. Meanwhile heaven is turned with changed tenor: for the wicked are burned then by divine fire. The creature groans, burning with the anger of God most high. More worthy, of noble stock and born of illustrious, and noble men under Antichrist defeated: living again from the command of God in the age, for a thousand years indeed, so that they may serve the saints and the High One, under a servile yoke, so that they may carry provisions on their neck; so that they may be judged again with the kingdom finished. Those who deny God, with the thousandth year completed, will perish from fire, with the mountains themselves speaking. All flesh is returned to the tombs and graves, they are submerged in hell, they drag punishments in the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory and worthy merit. Reward in perpetuity according to deeds to the tyrant. I am not able to comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find a name in this.

pass_b_english: Future inhabitants of heaven will be with God while Christ holds the beginning and sees all things from heaven. Let simplicity and goodness dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother, for you will receive back whatever you have done from him. This pleased Christ: to resurrect the dead with their bodies, and those whom fire has burned in the age, when six thousand years are completed and the world is finished. Meanwhile heaven is changed with a changed course, for the wicked are then burned by divine fire. The creation groans, burning with the anger of God Most High. Those more worthy, of noble stock and born of illustrious line, and noble men under Antichrist defeated: they will live again by God's command for a thousand years in the age, so that they may serve the saints and the High One, under a servile yoke, so that they may carry provisions on their neck; so that they may be judged again when the kingdom is finished. Those who deny God, when the thousandth year is completed, will perish by fire, with the mountains themselves speaking. All flesh is returned to the act in tombs and graves; they are plunged into hell and drag punishments in the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory and worthy merit. Reward in perpetuity goes to the tyrant according to deeds. I cannot comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find a name in this.
